record.question: State whether the following statements are true or false: (a) Suspension pending departmental enquiry against a Government Servant is not a punishment. (b) A suspended Government servant no longer retains a lien on the permanent post held by him substantively at the time of suspension. (c) Withholding of increment of a GS for his failure to pass any Department examination in accordance with the rules and orders governing the service to which he belongs or post which he holds or the terms of his appointment amount to penalty. (d) On the outcome of disciplinary proceedings any of the prescribed punishments is imposed on a GS, a record of the same should invariably be kept in his confidential roll. (e) The Disciplinary Authority can impose any of the major penalties specified in Rule 11 of CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 without holding inquiry. (f) At least 'WARNING' should be awarded when decided to penalize a GS as a result of Departmental proceedings. (g) A government servant appointed directly to Sub-Inspector cannot be reduced to Assistant Sub-Inspector, i.e. a post which he never held before, by way of punishment. (h) Government servant against whom disciplinary proceeding was drawn may take the assistance of any other Government servant posted in any office to present the case on his behalf. (i) A common/ joint proceeding can be held against Government servants working in the same office who have made complaint against each other. (j) Receiving bribe is a type of case which may merit action for imposing one of the major penalties.
options: True or False for each statement
record.explanation: The likely truth pattern is (a) True, (b) False (suspension does not end lien), (c) False (the specified withholding for failure to pass an examination is excluded from the Rule 11 penalties), (d) False (recording in the confidential roll is not invariably required), (e) False (major penalty normally requires inquiry), (f) False (warning is not a Rule 11 penalty), (g) False (reduction to a lower post can be a penalty), (h) True subject to the prescribed restrictions on a defence assistant, (i) True where the matter is covered by a common proceeding, and (j) True (bribe-taking may merit a major penalty). The actual answer choices are missing/blank, so no option index can be selected.
